title_en: Florence Pugh Texted Denis Villeneuve Asking to Be a Bond Villain After Robert Pattinson's Casting Went Viral
summary_en: Florence Pugh has thrown her hat in the ring in the hopes of becoming the next Bond villain after news of Robert Pattinson’s casting took over social media yesterday.
body_en:
Florence Pugh has thrown her hat in the ring in the hopes of becoming the next Bond villain after news of Robert Pattinson’s casting took over social media yesterday.
Robert Pattinson is your new James Bond , as revealed in an official video clip on November 16 that subsequently went viral. His casting has sparked no end of debate among fans , with some welcoming him into the fold with open arms, while others are arguing that they’d much prefer the likes of Henry Cavill, instead (though it seems Cavill wasn’t in the final list of actors who tested for the role).
Now that we have our new Bond, fans are going wild, sharing their personal picks for a villain to play opposite him — and even some A-List actors are vying for the part. Florence Pugh is one such actor, who admitted that she’d immediately texted director Denis Villeneuve out of interest in the part.
"Congratulations on finding your Bond, nice catch. Any villains the size of a 5ft 4in female?" she said at Elle’s Women in Hollywood event, recounting the message she’d sent him.
Pugh isn’t the only one gunning to be a Bond villain; Brad Pitt also expressed interest in the idea, telling Extra TV when approached with the topic, "You know what, I'd like to do that. I mean, my man Javier [Bardem] did it so well. It's tall shoes, but I'd take that on, yeah."
Pitt also had some kind words for Pattinson after learning of his casting, saying, “Is that right? You know what, I love this idea. I love what he's been doing. I love his choices, I think he's the real deal. That's great, good call."
Even former Bond actor George Lazenby weighed in on the news , giving Pattinson some sage advice as someone who has already played the part and experienced all the opinions that came with it.
“I hear they've announced the new James Bond,” Lazenby wrote in a post shared on social media. “Robert, welcome to the most exclusive club in the world. But remember to enjoy yourself. Let's see if you'll have [a] ‘This never happened to the other fella!’ moment. All the best, mate, George xx.”
Pattinson reportedly competed with Callum Turner, Jack Lowden, Josh O’Connor, and Nicholas Hoult for Bond, and was even given a far more lucrative deal for less films than other talent in the running. He auditioned for the role while filming for The Batman Part II was on pause — a project that now sits in limbo thanks to his latest gig.
While we likely won’t be seeing anything from Pattinson’s Bond for some time, fans can whet their appetites with Dune: Part Three , which comes to theaters this December.
